record.name: Saša Zdravković
record.title: Associate Professor
record.bio: Saša Zdravković received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Chemical Engineering from the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, in 2003 and 2006 respectively, followed by a Ph.D. from the same institution in 2011, with a dissertation on cellulase adsorption kinetics during hydrolysis of pre-treated wheat straw. After a two-year postdoctoral stay at the Graz University of Technology (2012–2014), he returned to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His group investigates enzymatic saccharification of lignocellulosic biomass, focusing on inhibition modelling, substrate structural characterisation after mild organosolv pre-treatment, and fed-batch reactor strategies. He teaches Biochemical Reaction Engineering and Industrial Biotechnology at undergraduate and graduate levels. The laboratory is equipped with a 5 L jacketed bioreactor, BET surface area analyser, UV-Vis spectrophotometer, and HPLC for sugar analytics.

access to 5 L bioreactor and HPLC sugar analytics for industrial partners

record.industry_experience: Zdravković conducted a six-month consultancy engagement with a regional bioethanol producer to assess the feasibility of switching from acid hydrolysis to enzymatic saccharification for their wheat straw feedstock line. He has also provided informal technical advice to two start-ups in the NTP Novi Sad ecosystem on enzyme dosing and substrate characterisation protocols.
record.notes: Zdravković is actively seeking a company partner with access to lignocellulosic biomass streams (agricultural residues, food processing by-products) for a planned industry contract or joint project starting in 2026. His Ph.D. student Nemanja Lazović will defend in late 2026 and may be available for an industrial position or industrial PhD continuation. The laboratory's HPLC instrument is available for fee-for-service sugar and organic acid analysis.
